narrative:

With 6-10 years overall, you fall into a group where employees are more likely to move on compared to those with very short careers. This signals to the model that you have built enough expertise to explore opportunities elsewhere.

Next, the model noted that you have not received any other job offers while at your current company. Surprisingly, this absence of external opportunities actually pulls the prediction slightly toward staying, as most employees who remain tend to also lack outside offers. However, this positive influence was not strong enough to offset the other factors.

Your length of time at this specific organization (1-5 years) was the third most influential element and pushed the prediction toward leaving. Employees predicted to stay are more evenly spread across experience levels here, but your relatively short tenure in this role aligns with patterns the model associates with higher turnover.

The organization should consider discussing your long-term goals with you and exploring ways to increase your sense of stability and growth within the company. You may want to reflect on whether your current path matches your career ambitions.
